wireInVerdicts.what: features/index.js — extend allRoutes with `...(isDevOrLocalEnvironment() ? addressLookupSpike.routes : [])` as a top-level, module-scope splice
wireInVerdicts.reason: features/index.js is a static ES module: `export const allRoutes = [...]` evaluates isDevOrLocalEnvironment() exactly once, the first time the module is imported by the process/test file, and the resulting array is then fixed for the lifetime of that module instance. Vitest does not reset modules between test.each() cases within the same describe/file. Main's original gate (`if (isDevOrLocalEnvironment()) { routes.push(addressLookupSpike) }`) lived inside router.js's async register(server), which reruns fresh on every createServer() call — so main's ported router.test.js (`#router EUDPA-390 address lookup spike gating`) calls `config.set('cdpEnvironment', X)` then `createServer()` in a loop across 8 test.each cases and expects each createServer() to re-check the config value at that moment. With the gate baked into a static allRoutes array, only the very first createServer() call in the file observes the real config state; every later test.each case with a different cdpEnvironment value gets the same frozen result (present or absent) regardless of what config.set() just did, and roughly half the 8 cases will fail.
wireInVerdicts.correction: Re-evaluate the gate at server-registration time, not at features/index.js's import time. Two ways to keep the rest of the port intact: (a) keep allRoutes static but move the conditional into router.js's/app/routes.js's register() function, e.g. `register: (server) => { server.route(isDevOrLocalEnvironment() ? [...allRoutes, ...addressLookupSpike.routes] : allRoutes) }` — mirrors main's original per-register() evaluation; or (b) make the exported list a function, e.g. `export const routesFor = () => [...staticRoutes, ...(isDevOrLocalEnvironment() ? addressLookupSpike.routes : [])]`, called from serviceRoutes.register(server) as `server.route(routesFor())`. Either keeps routes.test.js's exhaustive allRoutes snapshot working for the unconditional routes while making the conditional one respond live to config.set() in tests, matching main's actual behaviour (gate re-checked on every server start, not cached).

wireInVerdicts.what: controller.js — h.view(VIEW, { ...kit.base(PAGE_TITLE, { contentColumnClass: kit.surfaceClass('display') }), heading: PAGE_TITLE, ...extra })
wireInVerdicts.reason: kit.base()'s actual signature is `base = (title, { backLink, recoverableError = false } = {}) => ({ layout, pageTitle, backLink, sharedCopy, recoverableError, contentColumnClass: SURFACES.form })` — it destructures only backLink and recoverableError from its options argument and always returns contentColumnClass hard-coded to SURFACES.form (the two-thirds default). Passing `{ contentColumnClass: kit.surfaceClass('display') }` as base()'s second argument is silently ignored; base() still returns the two-thirds contentColumnClass, so the spread `...kit.base(...)` in the wire-in's proposed object would put the two-thirds value in the final view model regardless of the (unused) option passed in. The page would render in the narrow two-thirds column, not full-width — the opposite of the wire-in's stated intent and of main's original ungridded layout.
wireInVerdicts.correction: Every branch precedent that needs the wide surface (dashboard/controller.js, address-book/list/list.controller.js) sets `contentColumnClass: kit.surfaceClass('display')` as a SIBLING key in the object literal, placed AFTER the `...kit.base(...)` spread, so it overrides base()'s default rather than being passed into base() as an ignored option: `h.view(VIEW, { ...kit.base(PAGE_TITLE, { recoverableError }), contentColumnClass: kit.surfaceClass('display'), heading: PAGE_TITLE, ...extra })`.
